key_insight: CA-WCP adds class-aware, asymmetric conformal uncertainty bounds to 3D segmentation so volumetric predictions stay calibrated under distribution shift.
clinical_relevance: It can make multi-class medical image segmentation more trustworthy by quantifying when organ or tumor volumes may be over- or under-estimated.
method: Uses latent-space density-ratio weighting to handle covariate shift.
Applies separate lower and upper directional quantiles for volume bounds.
Scales bounds with class-specific asymmetry factors from false-positive and false-negative rates.
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2020 and a synthetic multi-organ CT shift benchmark, CA-WCP achieved class-wise 90% target coverage with 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals containing the nominal level and reduced interval width by 8–14% versus symmetric weighted conformal prediction.
watch_item: The approach adds extra calibration and prompt-generation steps, so performance and reliability may depend on the quality of validation data, shift estimation, and downstream model integration.
paper_title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
